description: Check a person's dietary supplements against NIH upper limits in one call. Give products as names, barcodes, NIH DSLD label IDs or ingredient lists; the service finds each label in the NIH Dietary Supplement Label Database, totals every vitamin and mineral (plus caffeine) per day, and compares the totals with NIH upper limits (UL) and RDA/AI for the age and sex, including pregnancy, lactation and infants, optionally with US average food intake added. Returns a plain-language agent_summary, above_ul/near_ul flags with severity, what each UL protects against, single-product changes that would fix an exceedance, the effect of adding candidate products, and warnings when an NIH label record looks wrong. Also: product search, barcode lookup, labels, reference values. Answers from its own label store when NIH is down. GET /v1/tools: tool definitions; GET /v1/guide: usage guide. Every number cites its source. Not medical advice; food, medications and drug interactions are not assessed (see Pocket services med-safety and fda).

rpc_types.notes: POST /v1/stack/analyze, /v1/products/search, /v1/products/lookup, /v1/products/get, /v1/nutrients/reference, /v1/tool; GET /v1/tools, /v1/guide, /v1/health, /v1/version, /openapi.json. All responses are JSON objects; errors are 4xx JSON with a stable error.code.

specs.notes: The release branch is what suppliers run (it deploys itself). Also served by every backend at GET /openapi.json; tool definitions at GET /v1/tools.

serving.backend: The dietary-supplement-analysis container (Node 22) behind the HA RelayMiner with the rest backend pointed at http://<backend>:8080. No auth toward the backend; callers cannot send headers. Needs outbound HTTPS to api.ods.od.nih.gov and a volume at /data for its label store.
serving.notes: Optional DSLD_API_KEY. Max 15 products plus 5 candidates per analyze call; names and barcodes are resolved server-side. DSLD calls are cached (labels 7 d, searches 1 d) and capped at 8 s per request; typical response under 3 s warm. Gateway operators: type passthrough, rpc_types ["rest"], relay_timeout 30s.
